offence_severity: Minimum 7 years, Maximum 10 years (Section 302 IPC) and life imprisonment (Section 120B IPC)
physical_harm: Death caused by hacking with a sharp-edged and lethal machete
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as part of conspiracy
key_evidence_accepted: The court accepted the material placed in the charge-sheet which gave rise to sufficient grounds of subjective satisfaction of prima facie case of alleged offences of conspiracy being hatched among the accused persons.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses by noting that the prosecution's witnesses did not provide any incriminating material against the appellant and that the credibility of the witnesses was not adequately addressed in the High Court's judgment.
trial_duration: Criminal case registered on 16th October, 2016; trial judgment dated 2nd January, 2018; High Court decision dated 22nd November, 2018; Supreme Court decision dated 1st July, 2019
legal_representation: Kamini Jaiswal, Abdul Rahiman, Shereef K.A., Ms. Rani Mishra, Jatinderpal Singh for the Appellant; Aman Lekhi, ASG, Ms. Shraddha Deshmukh, Kanu Agrawal, B. V. Balaram Das for the Respondent
investigation_status: Charge sheet filed on 21st April, 2017; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Dismissed the discharge application; High Court: Affirmed the trial court's decision; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that there was sufficient material to establish a prima facie case of conspiracy among the accused persons, including the appellant, and that the trial court correctly framed charges against the appellant based on the evidence and the charge sheet.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no material against the appellant, the charge against him was based on mere suspicion, and the High Court's judgment was erroneous and led to a miscarriage of justice.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the trial court has the power to sift and weigh evidence to determine whether a prima facie case has been made out against the accused, and that grave suspicion, not mere suspicion, justifies framing of charges.
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal & Ors. (1979) 3 SCC 4; Sajjan Kumar v. Central Bureau of Investigation (2010) 9 SCC 368; State v. S. Selvi and Ors. (2018) 13 SCC 455; Vikram Johar v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Ors. (2019) 6 SCALE 794
